message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I should ask my brother for an apology after what happened. Let me go through this step by step. First, the situation: My brother's girlfriend passed away, and her funeral was last week. We were all there, and her father was talking a lot about God. I whispered to my brother, "I wonder why God didn't save his daughter." I was just making a dark joke, I think. My brother glared at me, which he usually does when I make those kinds of jokes. After the funeral luncheon, we went home. My brother didn't talk to me. His friends came over, and when they asked how it went, I told them I didn't care about religion being shoved down my throat. My brother got really angry, slammed the remote on the table, and called me a dumbass. He said, "It was her father's church. You're twisting everything around to be some sort of oppressed victim, which is why everybody hates you. I can't believe you're this stupid." I told him I was going upstairs to try not to cry because I felt like he hated me. He accused me of guilt-tripping him, but I really did cry. When I came back down, I asked him to apologize because what he said was hurtful. He tried to minimize how awful I felt, saying I'm just a "cumbag." His friends said he took it too far, and he accused all of us of lacking empathy. So, the question is: Am I in the wrong (AITA) for asking my brother for an apology? Let me break this down. I made a comment about God not saving the girl, which was a dark joke. My brother took offense, and after that, he was angry and called me names. I felt hurt and cried, then asked him to apologize. He refused and minimized my feelings. I think about whether my initial comment was appropriate. At a funeral, especially when the family is talking about God, making a joke about God not saving someone could be seen as insensitive. Maybe I should have been more considerate of the situation. On the other hand, I was just making a joke, and I didn't mean any harm. But in a sensitive situation like a funeral, even a joke can be hurtful, especially when someone is grieving. When I told his friends about not caring for religion, that might have been a way to express my feelings, but it could have come off as dismissive of their beliefs, which might have upset my brother more. My brother's reaction was extreme. He called me names and slammed things. That's not a healthy way to handle conflict. But I did ask him to apologize, which is a reasonable request when someone has hurt you. However, he tried to minimize my feelings, which is not okay. It's important to acknowledge when someone is hurt, even if you think they're overreacting. I also think about the dynamics between us. My brother often glares at me when I make dark jokes, so maybe I should be more aware of how he reacts. But I also have the right to express myself, even if it's in a way that he doesn't like. In the end, I feel like I was within my rights to ask for an apology because his words were hurtful. But maybe I should have handled it differently, like talking to him when he was calmer or not bringing it up in front of his friends. I'm also considering whether I'm overreacting. My brother's friends said he took it too far, so maybe they agree that his reaction was excessive. That gives me some support that I wasn't entirely wrong to ask for an apology. But I'm still wondering if I should have just let it go, especially since he's grieving. Maybe I should have been more understanding of his emotions instead of focusing on my own hurt feelings. Overall, I think I was justified in asking for an apology because his words were hurtful, but perhaps I could have approached it more gently or at a different time. However, given the situation, I don't think I was entirely wrong to ask.
